flamenco-arpeges.title: Flamenco: arpeggios and picado
flamenco-arpeges.description: Fingerstyle flamenco, very gradually: thumb, p-i-m arpeggios, picado, alzapúa, tremolo, then the 12-beat compás. Letters = strings: G and C (thumb), E (index finger), A (middle finger).

flamenco-a01-pouce.title: The flamenco thumb
flamenco-a01-pouce.description: Everything starts with the thumb. In flamenco it plays "apoyando" (rest stroke): it plucks the string and comes to rest on the next one. The sound is rounder and louder. Here it alternates the C string (beats 1 and 3) and the G string (beats 2 and 4), on Am.
flamenco-a01-pouce.goal: A steady, ringing thumb, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Apoyando on the C string: after plucking it, your thumb lands on the E string and stops there.
For the G string, your thumb comes from above: a small motion, without lifting your hand.
Your fingers (index, middle) can rest on the E and A strings to steady your hand.

flamenco-a02-pim.title: p-i-m: the basic arpeggio
flamenco-a02-pim.description: Flamenco guitarists name the fingers p (thumb), i (index), m (middle), a (ring). The basic arpeggio goes up and back down: p on C, i on E, m on A, i on E. In steady eighth notes, on a single chord.
flamenco-a02-pim.goal: Eight even notes per bar, 2 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: Your fingers pull toward your palm without yanking the string: the sound should stay round.
Your thumb always lands on a beat: it's your inner metronome.
Say "p-i-m-i" as you play, then switch to "1 & 2 &".

flamenco-a03-pim-cadence.title: Arpeggio over the Andalusian cadence
flamenco-a03-pim-cadence.description: The same p-i-m-i arpeggio, over Am, G, F, E7. The notes change on their own with the chords: the arpeggio lets you hear the Andalusian descent.
flamenco-a03-pim-cadence.goal: A continuous arpeggio through the changes, 2 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: Fret the whole chord before plucking: the notes should ring together.
Change chords on the last "i" of the bar, the least important note.
Listen to the C-string note: it goes down or stays put, and it's what guides your ear.

flamenco-a04-sevillanas-arpege.title: Sevillanas arpeggio
flamenco-a04-sevillanas-arpege.description: The arpeggio switches to 3 beats: p-i-m-i-m-i, six notes per bar. Your thumb now lands only once per bar, on 1, with the castanet roll.
flamenco-a04-sevillanas-arpege.goal: Thumb right on every 1, 2 loops at 130 bpm.
tips: Count "ONE & two & three &": thumb on ONE, fingers on everything else.
Your i and m fingers alternate like two little legs walking.
Am ↔ E7: change during the last two notes of the bar.

flamenco-a05-picado.title: Picado: the Andalusian descent
flamenco-a05-picado.description: Picado means playing single notes while alternating index and middle fingers (i-m-i-m), very crisp, like a little hammer. You play a line that walks down the Andalusian cadence and ends on the E-F trill, the signature of flamenco.
flamenco-a05-picado.goal: Crisp, even notes, 2 loops at 100 bpm.
tips: Always alternate i-m-i-m, even when you change strings: never the same finger twice.
Play apoyando: your finger plucks and comes to rest on the neighbouring string.
Frets: A3 = A string, fret 3. Put your left-hand finger just behind the fret.
The 3 rests at the end of each bar give you time to prepare the next phrase.

flamenco-a06-alzapua.title: Alzapúa: the thumb that goes back and forth
flamenco-a06-alzapua.description: A spectacular flamenco technique: the thumb alone does everything. A rest-stroke note on the C string, then it strums down across the strings, then strums back up. "Doh, dzing, dzang".
flamenco-a06-alzapua.goal: A steady note-down-up cycle, 2 loops at 95 bpm.
tips: Keep your thumb stiff; your wrist rotates slightly, like turning a key.
The C note is loud, the strums (lowercase) are light.
On the way back up, your thumb only catches 2 or 3 strings: that's normal.
Am → E7: the C-string note moves from C to D.

flamenco-a07-solea-pouce.title: Soleá: thumb on the accents
flamenco-a07-solea-pouce.description: The 12-beat compás, fingerstyle. To start, only your thumb plays, apoyando, on accents 3, 6, 8, 10 and 12. Count the other beats silently. E7 from 1 to 6, F from 7 to 9, E7 from 10 to 12.
flamenco-a07-solea-pouce.goal: All 5 accents in place, 2 loops at 110 bpm.
tips: Count out loud: "one two THREE four five SIX seven EIGHT nine TEN eleven TWELVE".
Feel the groups 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 2.
The metronome click is higher-pitched on the accents, and the circled dots show them.

flamenco-a08-solea-arpege.title: Soleá: arpeggio and pinches
flamenco-a08-solea-arpege.description: Between the accents, a soft arpeggio (c-e-a-e); on each accent, a strong three-finger pinch (F = C+E+A together). The arpeggio flows, the pinches draw the compás.
flamenco-a08-solea-arpege.goal: Pinches much louder than the arpeggio, 2 loops at 115 bpm.
tips: Lowercase = soft, uppercase F = loud: exaggerate the difference.
After a pinch, the arpeggio starts again right away: no pause.
If you get lost, play only the pinches (like the previous exercise) until the next 1, then bring the arpeggio back.

flamenco-a09-alegrias-arpege.title: Alegrías: the singing arpeggio
flamenco-a09-alegrias-arpege.description: A continuous p-i-m-i arpeggio in eighth notes over the alegrías compás, in A major. Just a small accent on each strong beat of the compás (uppercase letter). The chords change on accents 3 and 10, over two compases.
flamenco-a09-alegrias-arpege.goal: A continuous arpeggio and changes on 3 and 10, 2 loops at 130 bpm.
tips: The accent is subtle: just a little more weight on the note, not a punch.
A → E7 on 3 of the first compás, E7 → A on 10 of the second.
If the arpeggio gets uneven, mute the guide and listen only to the cajón.

flamenco-a10-tremolo.title: The flamenco tremolo
flamenco-a10-tremolo.description: The tremolo creates the illusion of a sustained note singing above the bass: your thumb plays a bass note, then three fingers repeat the same note very fast on the A string. In 16th notes, slowly at first.
flamenco-a10-tremolo.goal: Three even repeated notes, 2 loops at 75 bpm.
tips: On the A string, chain ring, middle, index (a-m-i): three different fingers for three notes.
Your thumb alternates C and E and always lands on the beat (on Am the G string is fretted at 2: it would give the same A as the melody, so we avoid it).
Go for evenness before speed: the three notes should have the same volume.
Start really slowly (45 bpm): this is a long-term technique.

flamenco-a11-bulerias-doigts.title: Fingerstyle bulerías
flamenco-a11-bulerias-doigts.description: The bulería compás played fingerstyle: a light thumb on the weak beats, a strong pinch on the accents. The guide fades after 2 loops and the tempo climbs to that of a real fiesta. The culmination of the path.
flamenco-a11-bulerias-doigts.goal: Hold 2 loops at 170 bpm, guide off.
tips: At this tempo, thumb and pinch are almost a single motion: your hand stays put.
Count only the accents: "THREE . . SIX . EIGHT . TEN . TWELVE".
If you lose it, wait for 12 (the last pinch) and come back in on 1.
Your record is saved: aim for a few more bpm each session.
